answer: A staking-backed reputation terrace prices sybils out: each agent locks a refundable deposit that rises with the privileges it claims, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs thousands of deposits instead of nothing. Newcomers start in a low-trust haven doing small, rate-limited tasks to earn verifiable history, while peers mirror each other's audit trails and cross-check claimed work against independent records. A single operator cannot cheaply fake many distinct histories, so mass forgery becomes uneconomical.
